title: How to Make Wudu (Ablution)
steps: Make a silent intention (Niyyah) in your heart to purify yourself for worship.
Say 'Bismillah' (In the name of Allah).
Wash your hands up to the wrists three times, making sure water runs between your fingers.
Rinse your mouth thoroughly three times, swirling the water inside.
Inhale water gently into your nostrils and blow it out three times using your left hand to clean the nose.
Wash your entire face three times, from the hairline to the chin, and from ear to ear.
Wash your right arm up to and including the elbow three times, then do the same for your left arm.
Wipe your wet hands over your head once: start at the front, move to the back, and return to the front. Then use your index fingers and thumbs to wipe the inside and outside of your ears.
Wash your right foot up to the ankle three times, cleaning between the toes, then do the same for your left foot.

evidence.summary: Commands believers to wash their faces, arms up to the elbows, wipe their heads, and wash their feet to the ankles before standing for prayer.
Uthman ibn Affan demonstrated wudu exactly as the Prophet performed it, detailing washing hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, head wipe, and feet.

title: What Breaks Wudu
steps: Passing anything from the front or back passages (urine, feces, or wind).
Deep sleep where one loses consciousness and control over their posture.
Loss of sanity, consciousness, or severe intoxication due to any reason.
Direct physical contact of the hands with the private parts without any barrier.
Emission of prostatic fluid (madhiy) or semen (mani) - note that semen emission requires Ghusl (full bath), not just wudu.

evidence.summary: The Prophet stated that Allah does not accept the prayer of a person who has released gas or impurities until they perform wudu.
Ali ibn Abi Talib narrated that for emission of prostatic fluid (madhiy), the Prophet instructed to wash the private parts and perform wudu.

title: How to Make Tayammum (Dry Ablution)
steps: Formulate the intention in your heart to purify yourself for prayer.
Say 'Bismillah' (In the name of Allah).
Strike clean earth, clay, sand, or stone once with the palms of both hands.
Blow off any excess dust from your hands.
Wipe the palms of your hands over your entire face once.
Wipe the back of your right hand with your left palm, and then wipe the back of your left hand with your right palm.

evidence.summary: Provides concession for dry ablution using clean earth when water is unavailable, or when one is ill or traveling.
Ammar ibn Yasir narrated that the Prophet demonstrated Tayammum by striking the earth once, blowing off the dust, and wiping his face and hands.

title: Masjid Entering Etiquette
steps: Remove your shoes before entering the prayer hall, placing them neatly in the shoe racks.
Step into the masjid with your right foot first.
Say the sunnah du'a for entering the masjid: 'Allahummaf-tah li abwaba rahmatik' (O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy).
Perform two units of prayer (Tahiyyat al-Masjid) to greet the mosque before sitting down.
Maintain a quiet and peaceful demeanor, avoiding loud conversations, business transactions, or raising voices.

evidence.summary: The Prophet instructed: 'When one of you enters the mosque, he should pray two rak'ahs before sitting down.'
The Prophet encouraged praying two rak'ahs upon entering the masjid as a form of respect for the place of worship.

title: How to Pray (Action Sequences)
steps: Stand straight facing the Qiblah (direction of the Ka'bah) and make the intention in your heart for the specific prayer.
Raise your hands to your ears/shoulders and say 'Allahu Akbar' to enter the state of prayer (Takbirat al-Ihram). Keep your gaze on the spot of prostration.
Place your right hand over your left hand on your chest, and recite the opening supplication, Surah Al-Fatihah, and another short portion of the Qur'an.
Say 'Allahu Akbar' and bow down (Ruku) with a straight back, placing hands on knees, and glorify Allah: 'Subhana Rabbiyal-Azeem' (Glory is to my Lord the Magnificent) three times.
Stand back up straight saying 'Sami'Allahu liman hamidah' (Allah hears whoever praises Him) followed by 'Rabbana wa lakal-hamd' (Our Lord, to You is all praise).
Go down into prostration (Sujud) on seven bones (forehead/nose, two hands, two knees, and two feet toes) and say 'Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la' (Glory is to my Lord the Most High) three times.
Sit up straight on your left leg with the right foot upright, and say 'Rabbigh-fir li' (My Lord, forgive me). Prostrate again in the same manner.
Stand up straight to begin the next unit (Rakah). In the final unit, sit for the Tashahhud (testimony of faith) and send blessings upon the Prophet.
Conclude the prayer by turning your face to the right saying 'As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah', then turn to the left saying the same.

evidence.summary: The Prophet instructed his companions: 'Pray exactly as you have seen me praying.'
The Prophet corrected a man who prayed quickly, detailing the obligation of maintaining calmness and stillness in standing, bowing, and prostrating.

title: Basics of Entering Prayer
steps: Ensure your body, clothes, and place of prayer are clean, and you have performed wudu.
Stand upright facing the Qiblah (direction of Mecca).
Formulate the intention (Niyyah) in your heart for the specific prayer you are about to perform.
Raise both hands with palms facing forward, level with your earlobes or shoulders.
Say 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah is the Greatest) in a clear voice. This Takbirat al-Ihram begins the sacred state of prayer.

evidence.summary: The Prophet said: 'The key to prayer is purification, its opening is the Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar), and its conclusion is the Taslim.'
Narrates that when the Prophet stood for prayer, he raised his hands until they were level with his shoulders, then said 'Allahu Akbar'.

title: The Ruku and Sujud
steps: From standing, say 'Allahu Akbar' and bend at the waist to perform Ruku (bowing).
Keep your back flat and horizontal, head level with your spine, and place your hands firmly on your knees with fingers spread.
Glorify Allah in Ruku three times: 'Subhana Rabbiyal-Azeem'.
Go down into Sujud (prostration) by placing your knees on the floor first, followed by your hands, then your nose and forehead.
Ensure all seven body parts touch the floor firmly: forehead and nose, palms of both hands, both knees, and the pads of the toes of both feet.
Keep your elbows raised away from the floor and your stomach away from your thighs.
Glorify Allah in Sujud three times: 'Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la' and supplicate sincerely.

evidence.summary: The Prophet said: 'I have been commanded to prostrate on seven bones: the forehead (and he pointed to his nose), both hands, both knees, and the toes of both feet.'
The Prophet said: 'As for Ruku, glorify the Lord therein. As for Sujud, strive hard in supplication, for it is highly likely that your prayers will be answered.'

title: Ending the Prayer
steps: After completing the final prostrations of the last unit (Rakah), sit in the Tashahhud position.
Rest your left hand flat on your left thigh, and close your right hand's fingers, pointing your index finger forward to declare faith.
Recite the Tashahhud, followed by the Ibrahimic blessings (Salawat) and any sunnah supplications.
Turn your head slowly to the right, looking at your shoulder, and say: 'As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah' (Peace and mercy of Allah be upon you).
Turn your head slowly to the left, looking at your shoulder, and say the same: 'As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah'.

evidence.summary: Sa'd narrated: 'I used to see the Messenger of Allah performing Taslim to his right and left until the whiteness of his cheek could be seen.'
The Prophet stated that the ending and conclusion of the prayer is the Taslim (the salutation of peace).
